html:
The global order is being significantly shaped today by escalated US pressure on Iran, with Washington declaring an "economic D-Day" and threatening broad sanctions while also shifting diplomatic and military postures in the Gulf region.

North American Tensions: Canada announced 'dollar-for-dollar' retaliatory tariffs, as high as 50%, on US goods, the latest escalation in an ongoing trade war. This followed President Trump imposing 50% tariffs on many Canadian goods after trade talks broke down. On Truth Social, the president shot down assertions that US talks with Canada collapsed due to French language protections, stating "I would never interfere with Canadians speaking French!" Columnist Andrew Coyne discussed the reaction in Canada to Prime Minister Mark Carney rejecting a US trade deal.

Great Power Diplomacy & Conflicts: The CIA chief reportedly traveled to Moscow for unannounced talks, with flight tracking data confirming an American military aircraft's journey. Vatican foreign minister Archbishop Gallagher also began a visit to Russia, calling for the Ukraine war to end after meeting with Lavrov in Moscow. The UK will help Ukraine make long-range missiles by sharing classified tech information to aid in assembling weapons. Ukrainian drone strikes on Russian infrastructure on the Black Sea are disrupting grain and oil exports. Meanwhile, the Swedish military is seeking to take over a Russian-owned estate near its Muskö Naval Base, citing threats from Russian drones.

Global Economy & Markets: Oil prices fell for a second consecutive day, as traders perceived a reduced risk of renewed US military strikes on Iran after Washington threatened broader economic sanctions. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent declared an "economic D-Day" against Tehran but gave no timeline or details. Qatar announced a 30% reduction in its annual budget, a move expected to have global repercussions, potentially decreasing its worldwide investments. Iranian media reports indicated long lines and temporary closures at gas stations in Tehran, despite official assurances of stable fuel supply.

Iran War & Regional Security: President Trump is calling on world leaders to join his economic war against Iran, with new US sanctions seen by experts as a sign of Trump desperation. An oil tanker was struck by a projectile off Oman, with Yemeni armed forces announcing the targeting of a Saudi oil tanker. The US Navy informed Trump that all mines in the Strait of Hormuz have been removed, with US Secretary of State Marco Rubio stating the US now controls the waterway, leaving Iran without its leverage. However, Iran and Oman agreed on a temporary joint maritime corridor and a mine-clearing project in the Strait, though Iran insists Hormuz remains closed, despite the Oman route deal. The US starts returning staff to Middle East missions after Iran war evacuations, signaling fresh Iran hostilities are not imminent. The Trump Administration also sent a nuclear agreement with Saudi Arabia to Congress, with Reuters reporting Riyadh must recognize Israel.

MENA Geopolitical Shifts: The US officially removed Syria’s designation as a State Sponsor of Terrorism, a decision welcomed by Saudi Arabia, Jordan, Türkiye, UAE, and Kuwait. Mazloum Abdi, the commander-in-chief of the Syrian Democratic Forces (SDF), announced the dissolution of the group in a televised speech from Damascus, following its integration into the Syrian military, marking a major victory for Syrian President Ahmed al-Sharaa. Elsewhere, Palestinians launched a campaign titled #TheyLiedtoYou to counter the narrative of a ceasefire in Gaza, highlighting what they describe as Israel's ongoing genocide in the enclave. The UN condemns Israel's seizure and destruction of the UNRWA Kalandia Training Centre in occupied East Jerusalem.

Global Security & Public Health: A global crackdown on West African cyber-crime networks led to mass arrests, including 39 people in South Africa. Nigeria's president ordered a manhunt after kidnappers uploaded a victim video showing dozens of men, women, and children, and also ordered a rescue operation after a mass kidnapping at a mosque. The Trump administration halted all immigrant visa applications, with the state department moving to tighten restrictions and limit access to applicants deemed potentially reliant on US assistance. In the US, measles cases hit the highest point since the virus was eliminated, with two unvaccinated people dying in Pennsylvania amid declining vaccination rates.
